unclear_rules.note: The Tempest Rising game-wide note says 'Record it as a passive ability'. The ability-kinds tie-break (Passive or Triggered) would give triggered, since each attack causes a one-off zap. I followed the game note; the rules should say which wins.

With body size huge at t3, check A makes the Vimana super-heavy, overriding the armour_map's Aircraft-to-light mapping. The registry names only the Tempest Sphere and War Ender as lifted by size, and the game has no footprint data, so the size, and with it the armour class, rests on lore words.

unclear_rules.topic: Passenger seats in a placed garrison
unclear_rules.note: The registry leaves it to the coder whether the Lightning Rod's places count as the Thunderhead's seats, and that decides transport's requires. No seat role fits riders in a separate structure. Paired entries pairs passenger-firing with passenger-sets-weapon, while the garrison rule keeps a garrison whose riders fire out on carry-passengers; the two conflict for a garrison carried by a unit.

unclear_rules.topic: Doctrine that covers a whole class by naming every unit
unclear_rules.note: Engine Tuning's note lists all 14 Veti vehicles and aircraft by name. The Shared mechanics rule leaves off powers that change every unit of a class, but the registry explicitly asks for Engine Tuning to be recorded with commander-power. I followed the registry.

unclear_rules.topic: Air matchups in a game where only Air weapons reach fliers
unclear_rules.note: No word-list link means 'has an air-capable weapon' in this game. hits:low-air and hits:high-air both work in TR coding (every Air-line weapon lists both), but their generic meanings differ (most direct-fire weapons reach low air elsewhere). The rules do not say which to use.
The pattern summary describes shutting down until a relay exists again. Whether destruction on relay loss gives the same counterplay is not written. I linked the pattern, with a fit_note.
The task said the gate conflict needs the 2.0.0 notes, but those notes are silent on the Vimana's requirement. The registry's production-page rule settled it.

unclear_rules.topic: Weapon family for an undescribed energy shot
unclear_rules.note: The family tie-breaks (plasma or laser; plasma or cannon) need words on how the shot travels or what it fires. For the Vimana's cannon only the name and 'energy weapon' exist, so I used an analogy with a same-named defence turret; the rules do not cover analogies.
The rules do not say whether the job of units a button summons (Servitors the makers say can defend or scout) supports a role for the summoner at step 2, or only through its own parts.

new_mechanics.summary: A passive field that automatically strikes any enemy that attacks the unit from within a short radius with a small bolt of resistance-ignoring damage. Counterplay: attack from beyond the radius, or with units sturdy enough to shrug off the small return damage. Also on the Vimana (abilities/5).

An always-on aura stops enemy infantry inside it from receiving buffs, and any of them who die there rise as the owner's own units. Counterplay: fight from outside the aura, kill the aura carrier first, and avoid feeding infantry into it.

For a large price and a long cooldown, the unit brings a full, lasting unit (here a Caretaker) into play at its side, away from any factory; launch-drones covers only the short-lived escorts. Counterplay: kill the producer, punish the long wait between uses, and hunt the new unit before it starts work.

When an ally's buff lands on the unit, its spent ammunition comes back at once and refills faster while the buff lasts. Counterplay: catch it while its shots are spent, and kill or keep away the allies who would buff it.

The unit cannot receive one hostile status (Tempest Charge) and mends itself inside the hazard field that would normally inflict it. Counterplay: switch to damage that does not rely on that status, and draw it out of the field. Also on the Vimana (abilities/8); doctrine-given on both.

source_problems:
1. Neither unit page has a Verified tag, and both still carry the pre-release Upcoming banner. The Thunderhead page's speed (650) is older than the beta's 700; I used the 2.0.0 post's 900. Its health on the page (900) is also pre-release; the post gives 1300. Its price, sight and resistances have no newer confirmation.
2. The Vimana's price, speed, sight, health and resistances have no newer source. The 2.0.0 Veti notes name only one Vimana change (six Combat Servitors with Summon Caretaker).
3. Gate conflict: the Vimana page gives a bare Veti Eye requirement, while the Celestial Gate page (verified 1.8.0+57892) says Transcendent Awakening. Neither 2.0.0 post addresses it.
4. Arcing damage: the Arcing page's prose says 10 Omni, while its own perk box and the Ability page say 20. The Ability changelog says 1.6.0 set Arcing to 1700 radius 'on all sources', yet both boxes list some sources at 1800.
5. Garrison death: the Lightning Rod page says everyone inside dies when it is destroyed. The Garrisoning page quotes a 2024 designer remark (before the Veti existed) that garrisons drop their units with 40% health lost.
6. Caretaker cost: the Vimana page's prose says the Vimana makes Caretakers more cheaply than the Gate. Its ability box asks 3000 credits plus 8 population, against 2500 plus 2 at the Gate on the Caretaker page; the box's price may include the six Servitors added in 2.0.0.
7. Smaller oddities: the Lightning Rod infobox gives tier 3; the Vimana Limit perk box is commented out on the Vimana page; the Combat Servitor and Caretaker pages are also unverified.
8. Missing information: no page gives unit footprints (the UnitBox has no size field), and no source describes how the Blessed Golden Cannon's shot travels or what it fires.
9. All pages were already cached, so nothing was fetched in this session.
